definition: In historical evolutionary discussion, direct selection means selection that acts immediately on the trait or material in question, rather than producing it indirectly as a by-product of other changes. In the passage, it is contrasted with Darwin’s view that some features, such as mutual sterility, arise incidentally instead of being directly selected.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “direct selection” as selection “acting immediately on the trait or material” nor as “instead of” producing effects “as a by-product of other changes.”

The packet only provides a partial contrast: it states Darwin did not believe mutual sterility was produced “by direct selection in nature,” and it says selective “mean” rather than “acting directly upon the selected material,” but it does not supply the fuller immediate/by-product wording used in the definition.
The definition’s claim that Darwin’s alternative is “a by-product of other changes” is not supported by the packet’s language.
